Take this free CAT Circles online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Circles chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Circles tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Circles

Chords and tangents, circle theorems (angle at centre, semicircle), cyclic quadrilaterals, and arc/sector measures.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Angle at the centre = twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
  • Angle in a semicircle = 90°.
  • Tangent ⟂ radius at the point of contact; two tangents from a point are equal.
  • Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles sum to 180°.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting the tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
  • Using the inscribed angle where the central angle is needed (or vice versa).
  • Missing the cyclic-quadrilateral property.

quiz.title: CAT Circles Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Two parallel chords of a circle of radius 13 cm have lengths 24 cm and 10 cm and lie on OPPOSITE sides of the centre. The distance between them is
questions.explanation: Distances from centre: √(13²−12²)=5 and √(13²−5²)=12. Opposite sides ⇒ add: 5+12 = 17 cm.

questions.q: Two concentric circles have radii 13 cm and 5 cm. A chord of the larger circle touches the smaller circle. The length of this chord is
questions.explanation: The chord is tangent to the inner circle, so its distance from the centre = 5. Chord = 2√(R²−r²) = 2√(13²−5²) = 2×12 = 24 cm.

questions.q: Two chords AB and CD of a circle meet at an interior point P with PA = 8 cm, PB = 3 cm and PC = 6 cm. Then PD =
questions.explanation: Intersecting chords: PA·PB = PC·PD ⇒ 8×3 = 6×PD ⇒ PD = 24/6 = 4 cm.

questions.q: PA and PB are two tangents to a circle with centre O, and ∠APB = 70°. The measure of ∠AOB is
A horse is tied to a peg at a corner of a square field by a 14 m rope. Over how much area can it graze? (π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: At a corner the horse sweeps a quarter circle: ¼×πr² = ¼×22/7×14² = 154 m².

questions.q: A minor segment is cut off by a chord subtending 90° at the centre of a circle of radius 14 cm. Its area is (π = 22/7)
A right-angled triangle has legs 8 cm and 15 cm. The radius of its inscribed circle is
questions.explanation: For a right triangle the inradius = (a+b−c)/2 = (8+15−17)/2 = 3 cm.

questions.q: Two parallel chords of lengths 24 cm and 10 cm lie on the SAME side of the centre of a circle of radius 13 cm. The distance between them is
questions.explanation: Distances from centre: √(13²−12²) and √(13²−5²); same side ⇒ subtract ⇒ 7 cm.

questions.q: A chord subtends an angle of 60° at the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. Its length is
A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord of length 16 cm has length 6 cm. The radius of the circle is
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisects the chord, so radius = √(6²+8²) = √100 = 10 cm.

faq.q: What is the angle in a semicircle?
faq.a: A right angle (90°) — the diameter subtends 90° at any point on the circle.

faq.q: What is special about a tangent?
faq.a: It touches the circle at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
